name: Haley Moss
bio: Haley Moss is an attorney, artist and author who was diagnosed with autism at age three and didn't speak until she was four. In 2019 she became the first openly autistic female attorney in Florida, and she advocates for people with disabilities.
clues: I didn't speak until I was four years old.
I'm also an artist and teach college courses about autism.
In 2019 I became Florida's first openly autistic female lawyer.

name: Whoopi Goldberg
bio: Whoopi Goldberg is an actor, comedian and author who has dyslexia. She is one of the few entertainers to win an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar and a Tony, and she starred in The Color Purple.
clues: I have dyslexia and have talked about it to help kids who struggle with reading.
I started my career with one-woman shows on stage.
I starred in The Color Purple and won an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony.

name: Henry Winkler
bio: Henry Winkler is an actor famous for playing “the Fonz” on the TV show Happy Days. He has dyslexia, which wasn't diagnosed until he was an adult, and he co-wrote the Hank Zipzer books about a kid with dyslexia.
clues: I studied at the Yale School of Drama.
I didn't find out I had dyslexia until I was an adult, and I wrote kids' books about it.
I played Arthur “Fonzie” Fonzarelli on Happy Days.

name: Michael Phelps
bio: Michael Phelps is the most decorated Olympian of all time, with 28 medals, 23 of them gold. He has ADHD and has spoken openly about mental health.
clues: I have ADHD and have spoken about mental health.
At the 2008 Olympics I won eight gold medals.
I'm the most decorated Olympian ever, with 28 medals.

name: Billy Mills
bio: Billy Mills, whose Oglala Lakota name is Tamakhóčhe Theȟíla, won the 10,000-meter run at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics in one of the greatest upsets in Olympic history. He is still the only winner of that race from the Americas.
clues: I was an officer in the U.S. Marines.
Almost no one had heard of me before my Olympic race.
I'm an Oglala Lakota runner who won the 10,000 meters at the 1964 Olympics.

name: Zitkala-Ša
bio: Zitkala-Ša, whose name means Red Bird, was a Yankton Dakota writer, musician, educator and activist. Her books brought traditional Native American stories to many new readers, and she co-founded the National Council of American Indians to fight for Native people's citizenship and civil rights.
clues: I was also known as Gertrude Simmons Bonnin.
I wrote about being caught between two cultures.
My name means Red Bird, and I co-founded the National Council of American Indians.

name: N. Scott Momaday
bio: N. Scott Momaday was a Kiowa novelist and poet. His novel House Made of Dawn won the 1969 Pulitzer Prize and is considered the first major work of the Native American Renaissance.
clues: I received the National Medal of Arts in 2007.
My writing blends oral storytelling with the novel.
My novel House Made of Dawn won the Pulitzer Prize in 1969.

name: Charles Eastman
bio: Charles Eastman, also named Ohíyesa, was a Santee Dakota physician, writer and reformer. He worked as a doctor on reservations in South Dakota, wrote widely about Sioux history, and helped found the Boy Scouts of America.
clues: My Dakota name was Ohíyesa.
I worked as a doctor on reservations in South Dakota.
I founded Native American YMCA chapters and helped start the Boy Scouts of America.

name: Sharice Davids
bio: Sharice Davids is an attorney and former mixed martial artist who represents Kansas in Congress. In 2018 she became one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress and the first openly LGBTQ+ Native American in Congress.
clues: I used to compete in mixed martial arts.
I represent the Kansas City area of Kansas.
I'm one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress.

name: Liliʻuokalani
bio: Liliʻuokalani was the only queen and the last monarch of the Hawaiian Kingdom, overthrown in 1893. She was also a composer who wrote the famous song “Aloha ʻOe,” and while imprisoned she wrote her autobiography.
clues: I was born in Honolulu in 1838.
I wrote my autobiography while I was imprisoned.
I was the last queen of Hawaiʻi and wrote the song “Aloha ʻOe.”

name: Duke Kahanamoku
bio: Duke Kahanamoku was a Native Hawaiian swimmer who won five Olympic medals and held the world record in the 100-meter freestyle. He spread the sport of surfing around the world.
clues: I was born three years before the Hawaiian Kingdom was overthrown.
I won Olympic swimming medals in 1912, 1920 and 1924.
I'm a Native Hawaiian who made surfing popular around the world.

name: Nainoa Thompson
bio: Nainoa Thompson is a Native Hawaiian navigator and president of the Polynesian Voyaging Society. He guides traditional double-hulled canoes like the Hōkūleʻa across the Pacific using the stars, waves and wind instead of modern instruments.
clues: I'm president of the Polynesian Voyaging Society.
I navigate by reading the stars, waves and wind.
I sailed the canoe Hōkūleʻa across the Pacific without modern instruments.

name: Dwayne Johnson
bio: Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson, who has Black and Samoan heritage, played college football and became a pro wrestler before he grew into one of the highest-earning movie stars in the world.
clues: I played college football on a national championship team at the University of Miami.
My heritage is Black Nova Scotian and Samoan.
I'm a wrestler and movie star known as “The Rock.”

name: Alexandre Dumas
bio: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist and playwright, the grandson of an enslaved Afro-Caribbean woman. He is one of the most widely read French authors, famous for adventure novels like The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo.

photo.commons: Alexander Dumas père par Nadar - Google Art Project.jpg

clues: My father was a general born in Saint-Domingue, now Haiti.
I founded a theater in Paris.
I wrote The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo.

name: Nola Ochs
bio: Nola Ochs of Jetmore, Kansas, graduated from college in 2007 at age 95. Guinness World Records certified her as the oldest college graduate in the world at the time.
clues: I lived in Jetmore, Kansas.
I graduated from college in 2007.
I earned my college degree at age 95.

name: Julia Child
bio: Julia Child was a chef, author and TV host who brought French cooking to American homes. She published her first cookbook, Mastering the Art of French Cooking, at 49 and started her TV show The French Chef at 50.
clues: My TV show The French Chef premiered in 1963.
I published my first cookbook when I was 49.
I wrote Mastering the Art of French Cooking.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
bio: Gabriel García Márquez, known as Gabo, was a Colombian writer and journalist and one of the most important authors of the 20th century. His novel One Hundred Years of Solitude has sold more than 50 million copies, and he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.
clues: I left law school to become a journalist.
People across Latin America called me “Gabo.”
I wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude.

name: Isabel Allende
bio: Isabel Allende is a Chilean American writer called “the world's most widely read Spanish-language author.” Her novels include The House of the Spirits, and she received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2014.
clues: I became a U.S. citizen in 1993.
I received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2014.
I wrote The House of the Spirits.

name: Julia Alvarez
bio: Julia Alvarez is a poet and novelist who spent her early childhood in the Dominican Republic before her family fled to the U.S. Her novels include How the García Girls Lost Their Accents and In the Time of the Butterflies, and she writes the Tía Lola books for kids.
clues: I spent my first ten years in the Dominican Republic.
I write the Tía Lola books for young readers.
I wrote How the García Girls Lost Their Accents.

name: Juan Felipe Herrera
bio: Juan Felipe Herrera is a poet, writer and teacher whose childhood as the son of migrant farmworkers shapes his work. He was the 21st U.S. Poet Laureate and the first Latino to hold the role.
clues: I was the child of migrant farmworkers.
My children's book Calling the Doves won an award.
I was the first Latino U.S. Poet Laureate.

name: Antonia Novello
bio: Antonia Novello is a Puerto Rican physician who served as the 14th U.S. Surgeon General from 1990 to 1993. She was the first woman and the first Hispanic person in that role.
clues: I later served as New York State's Commissioner of Health.
I was a vice admiral in the Public Health Service.
I was the first woman and first Hispanic U.S. Surgeon General.

name: Sylvia Acevedo
bio: Sylvia Acevedo is an engineer who started her career at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory on the Voyager 2 team. She later led tech companies and served as CEO of the Girl Scouts of the USA, where she added more than 100 STEM and outdoor badges.
clues: I worked at Apple, Dell and Autodesk.
I started my career on NASA's Voyager 2 team.
As CEO of the Girl Scouts, I added more than 100 science and outdoor badges.

name: Benjamin Banneker
bio: Benjamin Banneker was a mostly self-taught Black mathematician, astronomer and surveyor in the 1700s. He helped survey the original borders of Washington, D.C., published popular almanacs, and wrote to Thomas Jefferson about slavery and racial equality.
clues: I was mostly self-taught and wrote popular almanacs.
I wrote letters to Thomas Jefferson about slavery and equality.
I helped survey the original borders of Washington, D.C.

name: Marian Anderson
bio: Marian Anderson was a contralto who sang everything from opera to spirituals. When she was banned from singing at Constitution Hall in 1939 because she was Black, she gave a famous open-air concert at the Lincoln Memorial instead, for a crowd of 75,000.
clues: I sang everything from opera to spirituals.
In 1939 I was refused permission to sing in Constitution Hall.
I sang a famous Easter concert on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial.

name: Arthur Ashe
bio: Arthur Ashe was a tennis champion and the first Black player selected for the U.S. Davis Cup team. He is the only Black man to win the singles titles at Wimbledon, the U.S. Open and the Australian Open, and he became an activist for civil rights and AIDS awareness.
clues: I was the first Black player on the U.S. Davis Cup team.
I spoke out about AIDS after getting HIV from a blood transfusion.
I'm the only Black man to win the men's singles at Wimbledon, the U.S. Open and the Australian Open.

name: Garrett Morgan
bio: Garrett Morgan was an inventor and businessman in Cleveland. He invented a protective “smoke hood” that he used to rescue workers in a 1916 tunnel disaster, and a three-way traffic signal in 1923.
clues: I also invented hair-care products and ran a company selling them.
I used my own invention, a smoke hood, to rescue workers in a tunnel disaster.
In 1923 I invented a three-way traffic signal.

name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
bio: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is a Nigerian writer of novels, essays and lectures, and a central figure in postcolonial feminist writing. She grew up in Nsukka, Nigeria, studied medicine briefly, and moved to the U.S. at 19 to study.

photo.commons: 2025-06-16 Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie no Fronteiras do Pensamento 2025 em São Paulo, 013 (cropped).jpg

clues: I studied medicine for a year and a half before switching to writing.
My first novel was Purple Hibiscus.
I'm a Nigerian writer famous for my essays and novels about identity and feminism.

name: Mary Seacole
bio: Mary Seacole was a Jamaican nurse and businesswoman who cared for soldiers during the Crimean War. She wrote the first autobiography by a woman of African descent in Britain and was voted the greatest Black Briton in 2004.
clues: My mother was a healer who ran a boarding house in Kingston, Jamaica.
I set up the “British Hotel” during the Crimean War.
I'm a Jamaican nurse voted the greatest Black Briton.

name: George Takei
bio: George Takei is an actor famous for playing Hikaru Sulu on Star Trek. As a child he and his family were held in an incarceration camp during World War II, and he is now a leading advocate for LGBTQ+ and immigrant rights.

photo.commons: George Takei GalaxyCon San Jose August-30-2026 270.jpg

clues: As a child, I lived in the Tule Lake camp during World War II.
I helped create a Broadway musical called Allegiance about Japanese American incarceration.
I played Sulu, the helmsman of the starship Enterprise.

name: Sunita Williams
bio: Sunita Williams is a retired Navy captain and NASA astronaut who has commanded the International Space Station twice. She has spent more time spacewalking than any other woman.
clues: I was a captain in the U.S. Navy.
My 2024 test flight turned into a stay of more than nine months in space.
I've spacewalked longer than any other woman.

name: An Wang
bio: An Wang was a Chinese American computer engineer and inventor who helped develop magnetic-core memory, an early type of computer memory. He co-founded Wang Laboratories, famous for its word processing machines.
clues: I helped invent magnetic-core memory for early computers.
My company was famous for word processing machines.
I co-founded Wang Laboratories.

name: Jhumpa Lahiri
bio: Jhumpa Lahiri is an author whose stories explore the Indian immigrant experience in America. Her first book, Interpreter of Maladies, won the Pulitzer Prize, and she now also writes in Italian.
clues: I moved to Rome and began writing in Italian.
My novel The Namesake became a movie.
My first book, Interpreter of Maladies, won the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Chloé Zhao
bio: Chloé Zhao is a Chinese-born filmmaker. For Nomadland, which she wrote, produced, edited and directed, she won the Academy Award for Best Director, becoming the first woman of color to win that award.

photo.commons: Chloé Zhao at the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival-68507.jpg

clues: My first feature film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.
I wrote, produced, edited and directed the film Nomadland.
I was the first woman of color to win the Oscar for Best Director.

name: Ludwig van Beethoven
bio: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist, one of the greatest in the history of Western music. He gradually lost his hearing but kept composing, writing some of his most famous works when he was almost completely deaf.
clues: I moved to Vienna at 21 and studied with Joseph Haydn.
I kept composing music even after I lost my hearing.
I wrote nine symphonies, including the famous Fifth and Ninth.

name: Chris Nikic
bio: Chris Nikic is a triathlete who in 2020, at age 21, became the first person with Down syndrome to finish an Ironman triathlon. He won ESPY awards for perseverance and as Best Athlete with a Disability.
clues: I won the Jimmy V Award for Perseverance at the ESPYs.
I finished an Ironman triathlon when I was 21.
I'm the first person with Down syndrome to complete an Ironman.

name: Hypatia
bio: Hypatia was a philosopher, astronomer and mathematician in Alexandria, Egypt, about 1,600 years ago. She was a famous teacher and is the first woman mathematician whose life is reasonably well recorded.
clues: My father, Theon, was also a mathematician.
I lived and taught in Alexandria, Egypt, about 1,600 years ago.
I'm the first female mathematician whose life is well recorded.

name: Emmy Noether
bio: Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who made major contributions to algebra and physics. Her theorem showing the link between symmetry and conservation laws is a foundation of modern physics. Because women were shut out of university jobs, she worked for years without pay.
clues: I first planned to teach French and English.
Because I was a woman, I worked at a university for seven years without pay.
My theorem connects symmetry in physics to conservation laws.

name: Valerie Thomas
bio: Valerie Thomas is a data scientist and inventor who worked at NASA for 31 years, developing the image formats used by early Landsat satellites. She invented the illusion transmitter, a 3D imaging device, and was inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2018.

photo.commons: NASA photo of data scientist Valerie L. Thomas.gif

clues: I graduated with honors in physics from Morgan State University.
I worked at NASA for 31 years on satellite images of Earth.
I invented the illusion transmitter, a device that creates 3D images.

name: Michael Ain
bio: Dr. Michael Ain is an orthopedic surgeon who practiced at Johns Hopkins Hospital. He has achondroplasia and is thought to be the first surgeon with the condition.
clues: I'm a doctor who operates on bones.
I practiced at Johns Hopkins Hospital.
I'm thought to be the first surgeon with achondroplasia.

name: Jennifer Arnold
bio: Dr. Jennifer Arnold is a neonatologist, a doctor who cares for newborn babies. She has skeletal dysplasia, and she shared her family's life on the TLC series The Little Couple.
clues: I trained in pediatrics at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center.
I'm a doctor who cares for newborn babies.
I starred in the TV series The Little Couple.

name: Sinéad Burke
bio: Sinéad Burke is an Irish writer and disability advocate who founded Tilting the Lens, a company that helps organizations become accessible. Her TED talk “Why design should include everyone” and her children's book Break the Mould made her widely known.
clues: I served on Ireland's Council of State.
I gave a TED talk called “Why design should include everyone.”
I founded Tilting the Lens and wrote the children's book Break the Mould.

name: Ellie Simmonds
bio: Ellie Simmonds is a British Paralympic swimmer who won two gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics at just 13, the youngest member of her team. She went on to win more golds and set world records in 2012 and 2016.

photo.commons: More British medals Ellie Simmonds (sq cropped).jpg

clues: I set a world record in the 400m freestyle at the London Paralympics.
I was the youngest member of Great Britain's team in 2008.
At 13, I won two Paralympic swimming gold medals in Beijing.

name: Linda Hunt
bio: Linda Hunt is an actress who won an Academy Award for playing Billy Kwan in The Year of Living Dangerously, the first person to win an Oscar for playing a character of the opposite sex. She later starred as Hetty Lange on NCIS: Los Angeles.
clues: My first film role was in Popeye.
I'm the narrator's voice in the God of War video games.
I won an Oscar for playing a man in The Year of Living Dangerously.

name: Peter Dinklage
bio: Peter Dinklage is an actor from New Jersey who has achondroplasia. He won a record four Emmy Awards for playing Tyrion Lannister on Game of Thrones, and his films include Elf and The Station Agent.
clues: I studied acting at Bennington College.
I played a children's book author in the movie Elf.
I won four Emmys for playing Tyrion Lannister.

name: Warwick Davis
bio: Warwick Davis is an English actor who has been acting since he was 11. He played Wicket the Ewok in Star Wars, the title role in Willow, and Professor Flitwick in the Harry Potter films, and he received a BAFTA Fellowship in 2025.

photo.commons: Warwick Davis Photo Op Nightmare Weekend Richmond 2023 (cropped).jpg

clues: I started acting when I was 11.
I played the title character in the movie Willow.
I played Wicket the Ewok and Professor Flitwick.
